      "startEvent": 235,
      "endEvent": 240,
      "contextStartEvent": 177,
      "contextEndEvent": 244,
      "speaker": "B",

      "form": "no",

      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "E193-208 presents a universal claim and offers one clean, uniquely religious good as its test. E235-240 then withholds defeat even if that test succeeds, requiring repeated successes. The children's-well analogy gives a reason for general caution, but that different question does not preserve the original universal claim against its counterexample."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1517,
      "endEvent": 1520,

      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The phrase challenges B's shared moral judgment by attributing it to Jesus, without establishing that dependence in this exchange. However, A previously offered historical and theological reasons at E357-398 and E1162-1169, and later limits the claim to historical scaling at E1635-1639. It is uncertain whether this use substitutes for reasons or summarizes them."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1911,
      "endEvent": 1918,
      "contextStartEvent": 1886,
      "contextEndEvent": 1956,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "This is the humanity coming through the religion.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B treats compassionate reinterpretation as humanity displacing religion. His proslavery quotations provide reasons, but do not establish that the image-of-God doctrines offered at E1162-1169 cannot motivate abolition. Calling contrary texts vague may exclude counterevidence, yet this could also be an answerable interpretation dispute; A immediately renews his doctrinal case at E1921-1956."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2428,
      "endEvent": 2438,
      "contextStartEvent": 2407,
      "contextEndEvent": 2441,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "The more kind of the Christian, the less they've read.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "identity",
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The maxim turns kindness into evidence of reduced biblical reading, without supplying evidence for that relationship. Earlier harmful-text examples support criticism of particular doctrines, not this general claim about readers. E2430-2438 risks dismissing compassionate Christians as counterexamples by definition, although it remains unclear whether B intends unconditional exclusion rather than an empirical generalization."
    }
  ],
